minor.issue: Bare `except Exception` on line 648 re-raises raw exception text in 502 detail (same pattern as iter-3 AI endpoint). Consider stripping provider error specifics.
Invalid style_guide silently falls back to 'chicago' (per spec) but the response echoes the *fallback* key without a warning header — a client passing 'klingon' has no way to know it was overridden.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: Variable shadowing — line 106 declares `const [document, setDocument] = useState(null)` which shadows the global `document` object inside the entire component. Line 353 then calls `document.createTreeWalker(...)` and throws `TypeError: document.createTreeWalker is not a function` because it resolves to the React state (the loaded document model) rather than the DOM. Reproduction: load editor, run copy-edit, click Accept on any issue → React red-screen error overlay appears and Accept All also crashes. Fix applied during testing: changed line 353 to `window.document.createTreeWalker(...)`. Verified: Accept, Accept All, Reject, filter, Reject All all work after the fix.

issues: When all issues are accepted/rejected the 'Manuscript is clean — no issues remain' green banner stays visible even after the user re-runs the pass (replaced only on next API response). Acceptable but slightly stale.

action_items: REVIEW the one-line fix I applied at /app/frontend/src/pages/EditorPage.js line 353 (`document.createTreeWalker` → `window.document.createTreeWalker`). A cleaner fix would be to rename the React state from `document` to `documentData` (or similar) throughout the component to remove the shadowing entirely — preferred long-term. The state `document` is referenced in many places in EditorPage.js; renaming requires care.
Consider sanitising the 502 detail string in run_copyedit (echoes raw provider exception text).
Optional: return a `warning` field or HTTP header when an invalid style_guide is coerced to chicago, so clients can surface a hint.
critical_code_review_comments: EditorPage.js: `const [document, setDocument] = useState(null)` shadows the global DOM object. This is the root cause of the runtime crash on accept-issue. Rename the state variable to e.g. `documentData` / `docMeta` to eliminate the entire class of bugs (any future `document.xxx` reference would silently break).
ai_copyeditor.py.run_copyedit_pass: no timeout around chat.send_message — a hung Claude call will tie up a FastAPI worker indefinitely. Wrap with `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=120)`.

ai_copyeditor.py: `re.search(r"\{[\s\S]*\}", raw)` is greedy — if Claude wraps JSON in commentary with multiple braces, the match grabs from first `{` to last `}` which still parses but can include trailing junk. Prefer `json.loads` of the stripped body and only fall back on regex.

EditorPage.js: applyCopyEditFix walks text nodes and stuffs the entire replaced string into nodes[0], then clears the rest. This preserves text but destroys inline formatting (bold/italic spans) within the targeted paragraph — accepting a fix on a bolded sentence will silently strip the <strong> tags. Worth a regression test.

EditorPage.js handleAcceptAll: applies fixes in reverse paragraph_index order but does NOT account for multiple issues sharing the same paragraph_index — the second fix's `original` substring may have been replaced/shifted by the first. Some skips on accept-all are expected; observed `Applied 10 fixes` with `0 skipped` only because the test prose had largely disjoint substrings.

rca_of_the_issue: RCA — Accept/Accept-All crash: EditorPage.js line 106 declares `const [document, setDocument] = useState(null)` which shadows the global `window.document` for the entire component scope. Line 353 calls `document.createTreeWalker(target, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT, null)` expecting the DOM API; at runtime `document` resolves to the React state (a plain object or null), so `.createTreeWalker` is undefined → TypeError → React error overlay → all subsequent clicks blocked. Reproduction: 1) load any document in the editor, 2) click Run Full Edit, 3) wait for issues, 4) click any Accept button → red runtime error overlay appears with `TypeError: document.createTreeWalker is not a function`. Mitigation: minimal one-line patch to `window.document.createTreeWalker`. Permanent fix: rename the React state variable `document` to `documentData` (or `docState`) throughout EditorPage.js — current line 106 + every reader of `document` and `setDocument` would need updating. This also future-proofs against any other accidental `document.<DOM_API>` calls.
